target.title: feat: render inline web chat widgets via capability-gated show_widget tool
target.body:
Closes #101790

## What Problem This Solves

Agents in the web chat can only answer in text and markdown. For content that is inherently visual — flow diagrams, small dashboards, comparisons, interactive explainers — a rendered inline widget communicates far better, and OpenClaw already ships the rendering substrate (the Canvas plugin's sandboxed embed pipeline). What was missing is a first-class tool for "render this markup inline in the chat transcript," and the underlying capability such a tool needs: a way to offer a tool only where the user's client can actually render its output. Today every gateway client (web UI, iOS, Android, macOS, CLI) collapses to the same internal message channel at tool-assembly time, so a web-only tool would have appeared — and dead-ended — on phones and terminals too.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two parts, deliberately layered:

**Client-capability-gated tool availability (generic core seam).** Gateway clients already declare capability flags at connect (`GATEWAY_CLIENT_CAPS`, previously only `tool-events`). This adds an `inline-widgets` capability that the browser Control UI declares, stamps the connected client's caps into the per-run message context at `chat.send` dispatch (mirroring `GatewayClientScopes`), and threads them through the run/queue/compaction paths into tool assembly. Tools — core or plugin — can declare `requiredClientCaps`; `createOpenClawTools` drops any tool whose required caps the originating client did not declare. Channel runs (Telegram, WhatsApp, …) have no gateway client and therefore no caps, so gated tools are simply absent there, and `tools.allow` cannot resurrect them (capability is a hard availability fact, not policy). Queue collect-mode batching keys on caps so runs from different surfaces don't merge. Additive protocol only: one new capability string, no version bump, no new config keys.

**`show_widget` tool (Canvas plugin).** The agent passes a `title` plus `widget_code` (`<svg …>` or an HTML fragment, ≤256 KiB). The plugin wraps it in a minimal HTML shell and persists it through the existing Canvas document store — bounded to 32 documents per session scope, oldest evicted — and returns the canvas preview handle the web chat already knows how to render, so the widget appears inline from the tool call itself and survives history reload with zero new UI rendering machinery.

**Security model** (hardened through two structured-review cycles):
- Widget iframes never get `allow-same-origin`: the preview carries a sandbox ceiling that caps the operator's global `embedSandbox` mode, enforced on both the inline preview and the sidebar open path.
- The Canvas host serves widget documents with a `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts` response header, so navigating to the hosted URL directly also runs the widget in an opaque origin rather than the Control UI origin.
- The widget document's own CSP (`default-src 'none'`; inline style/script; `data:` images) blocks external fetches and resource loads; the Control UI page CSP (`default-src 'self'`, no `frame-src`) additionally restricts where embedded frames can navigate. Scripts remain allowed by design — widgets are interactive — with the residual self-navigation limitation documented on the docs page.

## User Impact

Agents talking to the web Control UI gain a `show_widget` tool and can answer with rendered, optionally interactive, self-contained widgets inline in the chat. Users on Telegram, WhatsApp, the CLI, or the native apps see no change: the tool does not exist for those runs, so agents cannot call it into a void. Plugin authors get a documented, generic way to ship surface-conditional tools (`requiredClientCaps`), and native apps can adopt the widget surface later by declaring the capability. No configuration changes are required; the existing `gateway.controlUi.embedSandbox` tiers keep applying, with widgets capped below `trusted`.

## Evidence

- Capability gating: `src/agents/openclaw-tools.client-caps.test.ts` (absent caps exclude, superset includes, channel runs exclude, `tools.allow` cannot resurrect), `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.client-caps.test.ts` (collect-mode batching keys on caps), `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts` (ctx stamping; 270 tests), `src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.test.ts` (caps survive descriptor caching).
- Widget tool: `extensions/canvas/src/widget-tool.test.ts` (validation, SVG/HTML wrapping with CSP meta, opaque ids, per-scope eviction, manifest sandbox marker), `extensions/canvas/src/host/server.test.ts` (sandbox-marked documents get the CSP sandbox header and skip live reload; unmarked documents unchanged).
- Web UI: `ui/src/api/gateway.node.test.ts` (Control UI declares `inline-widgets`), `ui/src/lib/chat/tool-display.node.test.ts` (sandbox ceiling math), `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.node.test.ts` (canvas handle extraction incl. sandbox; sidebar conversion preserves the ceiling), `ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts`.
- `pnpm build` green with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`; docs map/MDX/link checks green; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files; `git diff --check` clean.
- Structured autoreview ran until clean: two P1 findings surfaced and were fixed with regression tests (sidebar path dropping the sandbox ceiling under `trusted` mode; hosted widget documents executing as the app origin when opened directly), final review reported no actionable findings.
- Focused proof ran locally (hosted CI verifies the full gates at the exact head); remote box warmups were queued at the time, noted per validation policy.
